subject: Hosted API pricing qualification — expected monthly tokens + peak TPS
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia White <olivia.white@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-07T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification — expected monthly tokens + peak TPS

Hi Olivia — great call today, thanks for walking us through the integration and traffic patterns. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can put together a realistic hosted-API quote and cost estimate.

Call recap (high level)
- Use case: conversational assistant + contextual retrieval for transaction support across mobile/web.
- Typical prompt+response size: ~800 tokens per interaction (average), but a good portion of traffic is shorter confirmations (~200–400 tokens).
- Current plan: pilot across 3 markets, then expand to global.

Key asks for pricing estimate
1) Expected steady-state monthly token volume (rough range is fine): e.g., 10M / 50M / 200M+ tokens per month.
2) Peak TPS (we care about token TPS and RPS). If you can share peak concurrent requests or typical peak requests/sec, that helps.
3) Target unit economics / acceptable $ per 1M tokens (if you have an internal target we should know).
4) Any fixed monthly budget range to align discounts/commit suggestions.

From our side, to get within your budget we typically look at a few levers: batching/prefix caching, using a quantized model variant for high-throughput paths, and committed volume pricing (reserved tokens). If your target $/1M tokens is in the $300–$500 range we can usually get close with a small committed discount + batching; if lower than $200 we need to discuss Dedicated or on-prem options for predictability.

Next steps
- If you can send a top-level monthly token estimate and an expected peak requests/sec window (or peak token TPS), I’ll run a few pricing scenarios and share a rough hosted-API estimate + recommended config.
- Marissa (cc) will be available to do a quick perf plan if you want us to validate latency under your peak.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Olivia White <olivia.white@fintechco.com>

Date: 2026-06-08T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — expected monthly tokens + peak TPS

Thanks Ben — quick answers below and I attached a traffic forecast spreadsheet for June–Dec (high-level).

1) Expected monthly tokens (steady state after pilot, month 3+): ~120M tokens/month (we expect ramp from 20M in month 1 to ~120M by month 3).
2) Peak TPS: our peak is roughly 25 requests/sec during business-hours bursts; average request payload (prompt+response) ~150 tokens — that implies peak token TPS ~3,750 tokens/sec. We also see short bursts up to ~40 RPS but those are rare.
3) Target unit economics: our procurement team is aiming for ~$350 per 1M tokens as an internal target for hosted endpoints.
4) Budget range: initial target budget for hosted API during pilot/rollout is $20k–$30k/month, but we can consider higher if the value is there — need to close the gap to execs.

Attachment: fintechco_traffic_forecast_v1.xlsx

Happy to hop on another 15-min call if you want to walk the numbers together.

—Olivia
Olivia White
Head of Product, FintechCo
olivia.white@fintechco.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia White <olivia.white@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-08T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — expected monthly tokens + peak TPS

Thanks for the details and the spreadsheet, Olivia — this is really helpful. Quick math / implications and a couple of options to align to your budget.

Numbers (straight hosted estimate)
- 120M tokens/month at your target $350 per 1M tokens -> $42,000/month (120 * $350).
- That is above the $20k–$30k target range you called out.

Options to bridge the gap
1) Committed volume discount (reserved monthly commit): with a 6–12 month commit we can typically offer tiered pricing that reduces the $/1M by ~15–30% depending on the commit size. For example, a 6-month commit around 120M/month could get you to roughly $245–$300 per 1M tokens.
2) Traffic optimizations: batching, prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, and pushing smaller confirmation flows to a smaller model variant — these can reduce average tokens/interaction by 15–20% in many customers. Marissa can run a quick eval to validate.
3) Mixed model strategy: route high-sensitivity interactions to a higher-quality model and lower-cost interactions to a quantized/cheaper variant.
4) Dedicated/Reserved capacity: if predictability and unit cost are top priorities, our Dedicated offering (reserved GPU capacity) often yields the best $/1M economics at scale. That also gives you SLA-backed latency targets.

Proposed next steps
- I’ll put together 2 hosted pricing scenarios: (A) no commit at $350/1M, (B) 6-month committed pricing with a modeled 20% discount and optimized token estimate (assume 20% reduction from batching).
- Marissa — can you confirm whether the 150-token average in your forecast is an upper-bound or representative? Also can you run a quick expected savings chart if we apply 20% token reduction?
- Olivia — if you’re open, we can schedule a 15–20 minute call this week to walk the scenarios and procurement timing.

I’m attaching a placeholder pricing shell to show the structure (not final quote): redwood_pricing_shell_v1.pdf.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia White <olivia.white@fintechco.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-09T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — expected monthly tokens + peak TPS

Olivia — quick note from the SE side. Good news: 3,750 token/sec peak is well within hosted capacity for the models we discussed, assuming reasonable concurrency/connection handling on your side. A couple of practical recommendations:

- Autoscaling: set your request-level concurrency target to 50–100 concurrent requests with a 30s cooldown; this will smooth bursts (we’ll provide an autoscale policy template).
- Caching: if you have repeated prompts (e.g., common confirmation text), prefix caching can reduce tokens by ~10–25% with minimal infra changes.
- Token reduction: in our experience with similar customers, conservative engineering changes + batching can yield ~15–20% token savings during pilot.

I’ll start a quick sizing test plan — if you can give me a CSV of sample request sizes (or we can sample from your forecast), I’ll simulate latency at 25 RPS and 40 RPS with the recommended batching settings and report back.

Happy to coordinate a short call to walk the perf plan.

—Marissa

Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
